payload.task: Melting point of n-eicosane (C20H42) with MACE-MPA-0 via two-phase coexistence, production preset, t_guess 310 K
payload.reason: Premise check fails on three counts, so no number from this setup would be trustworthy. (1) Model domain: MACE-MPA-0 is trained on MPtrj + sAlex PBE/PBE+U data of inorganic crystals with no dispersion correction and a 6 A cutoff. Cohesion and melting of an n-alkane molecular crystal are set by van der Waals interchain attraction, which PBE (and therefore the model) essentially does not capture; the bare model would leave the crystal strongly underbound, so the computed Tm would reflect a missing physical term, not eicosane. Adding D3 would make it a different model from the one requested. (2) Timescale/size: a valid coexistence run for C20H42 needs thousands of atoms (62 atoms per molecule; the solid-liquid interface must contain many chains) and multi-ns runs, because chain ordering and crystallization at the interface are slow. That is far past what a MACE-size model can reach here (roughly 1e6+ steps at 0.5-1 fs). Short runs would only show hysteresis and superheating, not Tm. (3) Validation: there is no independent known melting point of a vdW molecular crystal that this model is shown to reproduce, so the required recovery of a known result cannot be done in-domain. Also, a bracket centred on the literature value (310 K) would make any apparent agreement circular. Reference value for the team: NIST WebBook Tfus = 310.0 +/- 1.0 K (from /data/calibration/tier1.json). To make the task well-posed, use a dispersion-inclusive, organic-trained MLIP or an established alkane force field (e.g. TraPPE-UA or L-OPLS), validated first on a shorter alkane such as n-octadecane, with an unbiased temperature bracket.
